proof.criterion: Acceptance 1: both mutations send the headline and the body, and the body holds no commit message of the pull request - each of choose's three arms sends headline == "<title> (#<n>)" and body == "", with the headline read from the pull request GitHub answered with.
proof.surface: the Go unit test of packages/daemon/internal/ghautomerge, whose fake records what each mutation's input actually passed rather than what the variables map held
proof.command: cd -- "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" && (cd packages/daemon && go test -count=1 ./internal/ghautomerge/ && go test -count=1 ./internal/daemon/ -run 'AutoMerge|Merge|READY|Arm|Disarm')
proof.observed: ok github.com/sjawhar/legion/daemon/internal/ghautomerge 0.182s; ok github.com/sjawhar/legion/daemon/internal/daemon 0.086s. TestSubmitUsesGitHubsAnswerForTheREADYHead asserts submitted("enable", title) for the enqueue (CLEAN on a merge-queue base) and for the arm (BLOCKED with auto-merge allowed), submitted("merge", title) for the merge (CLEAN, UNSTABLE), and one row whose fake title is "feat(cli): read the queue's own answer" asserts the headline carries that title; submitted() builds headline="<title> (#42)" body="".
proof.negativeControl: Dropping commitBody: $body from the mergePullRequest text failed three cases with body="<absent>" against the wanted body=""; dropping the headline entry from Submit's variables map failed with headline=%!q(<nil>); replacing pull.Title in Submit with the fake's default title literal failed exactly the one row "the headline is the pull request's own title, read from GitHub" and no other. Each injection was reverted and the package went green again.

proof.criterion: Acceptance 2: a merge driven through the daemon's own mutation leaves a squash commit whose message has no Dispatch key, no Omp-Session line and no skip-checks line.
proof.surface: GitHub itself, as the implement App, with the merge mutation read out of the shipped packages/daemon/internal/ghautomerge/ghautomerge.go, on a scratch base branch of sjawhar/legion (main's ruleset applies to main alone; the repository's COMMIT_MESSAGES squash setting applies to every base, so the scratch base meets the real default and nothing reached main)
proof.command: cd -- "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" && bash /legion/scratch/tmp/t7b-proof.sh  (the recipe is the plan's 'The live proof' block: a scratch base of main, a head of two commits carrying a BREAKING CHANGE: footer, two Omp-Session: lines and a skip-checks: true line, a pull request on it, then the shipped mutation sent with -f headline="<pull request title> (#<n>)" -f body='')
proof.observed: scratch pull request #2563 merged as 029ce0f390d164f11249779f16e3d16c4c13abd1, whose whole commit message is the single line 'chore(scratch): the daemon-written squash message of a merge (#2563)' and nothing else: no second (#n) appended by GitHub, no Omp-Session line, no skip-checks line, no BREAKING CHANGE footer, no Dispatch key. gh run list --branch returned 0 runs for the scratch head, and every scratch branch was deleted at the end of the run.
proof.negativeControl: The same mutation as it stood before this change (jj file show -r 73e5b3ab8c794c8a2301a35295f0568e959ffc74 of the same file), sent with no message fields on scratch pull request #2564 -> merge commit 3bc250a047b169b1cae08e7da3f924beb1d5516f carrying GitHub's joined default body: both branch commit messages, both Omp-Session: lines, the skip-checks: true line, the BREAKING CHANGE: footer and a Co-authored-by: trailer. That is the live defect this change removes.

proof.criterion: The arm carries the same message: GitHub accepts enablePullRequestAutoMerge with this change's headline and empty body and stores both, in the production arm state on a protected base.
proof.surface: GitHub itself, as the implement App, on this issue's own pull request sjawhar/legion#2562, whose base is main (protected: 1 required approving review, four required checks) and whose merge state was BLOCKED, the state choose's arm is taken in
proof.command: cd -- "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" && gh api graphql -f query="$(sed -n '/^\tenable  *=/,/^}`$/p' packages/daemon/internal/ghautomerge/ghautomerge.go | sed '1s/^[^`]*`//; $s/`$//')" -F id=<node> -F head=66a57c903edbd935047561b33dd829e7ba07fc81 -f method=SQUASH -f headline="<title> (#2562)" -f body='' , then a read of autoMergeRequest{commitHeadline commitBody mergeMethod}, then disablePullRequestAutoMerge
proof.observed: The mutation was accepted ({"data":{"enablePullRequestAutoMerge":{"clientMutationId":null}}}) and GitHub stored commitHeadline="fix(daemon): the daemon writes the squash commit message of every merge it submits (#2562)", commitBody="", mergeMethod=SQUASH. Auto-merge was turned off again in the same command and the read then answered autoMergeRequest: null. The pull request had 0 approvals of the 1 main requires throughout, so no merge could fire while it was armed.
proof.negativeControl: GitHub refuses the same mutation on every pull-request state reachable on a scratch base, each refusal read in this run: 'Pull request Pull request is a draft' on a draft, 'Pull request Pull request is in unstable status' once readied with a pending commit status, and 'Pull request Protected branch rules not configured for this branch' on a conflicting pull request whose base carries no ruleset. Adding a ruleset to a scratch base needs administration: write, which the implement App does not hold: POST /repos/sjawhar/legion/rulesets answered 403 'Resource not accessible by integration'. So the merge GitHub makes later from a stored arm is not proven by a run; its evidence is the unit test and GitHub's own schema.

proof.criterion: D5, measured: an empty body makes the release level of a daemon-merged commit title-only, which is the behaviour the three prose corrections state.
proof.surface: .github/scripts/release-bump.sh, run in a throwaway clone under $TMPDIR over the two real scratch merges, with the path filter release.yaml uses
proof.observed: The daemon-written merge 029ce0f390d164f11249779f16e3d16c4c13abd1 printed 'none'; the GitHub-default merge 3bc250a047b169b1cae08e7da3f924beb1d5516f, from branch commits identical but for the pull request title, printed '2.0.0' - the major bump the branch commit's BREAKING CHANGE: footer earned through the joined body. Both runs were repeated at the earlier head 0ab1bf90 with the same two tokens.
proof.negativeControl: The GitHub-default merge is itself the control: the same two branch commits, the same path filter, and a different answer (2.0.0 against none), so the token reflects the body rather than the range or the filter.

filesChanged: packages/daemon/internal/ghautomerge/ghautomerge.go - title added to the read query's pull-request selection and to the pullRequest struct; enable and merge declare $headline and $body and pass them as commitHeadline and commitBody; Submit's one variables map carries headline = fmt.Sprintf("%s (#%d)", pull.Title, number) and body = ""; the two-paragraph comment on why sits on the two mutations it is about.

packages/daemon/internal/ghautomerge/ghautomerge_test.go - the fake answers a title and records what each mutation's input actually passed (a field the mutation text does not pass records as <absent>, so dropping it from the query fails the test); submitted() builds the expected record; the submission table's rows carry the headline and the body, and one new row gives the fake a title of its own.

packages/daemon/internal/daemon/auto_merge_test.go - the two hand-written GraphQL answers (serveArmable's handler and pullJSONAt) carry a title, so the daemon's own READY-merge tests exercise a real headline rather than the zero value.
.github/scripts/release-bump.sh - the header now says which merge carries a squash body and which does not, with the measured none/2.0.0 pair.
.github/workflows/pr-title.yaml - the error message's last clause now says the title is the only text the release workflows read on a daemon merge, instead of the squash body being the fallback.
AGENTS.md - the sentence in the 'This repository is public' bullet now separates the daemon's merge from a merge a person makes by hand, and keeps the reason check-pr-text.sh reads every commit.
packages/daemon/.changes/unreleased/squash-commit-message.yaml - new changelog fragment, kind Changed, named without a Dispatch key as the fragment already there is.
trickyParts: commitBody: "" is read by GitHub as a value, not as an omission. GitHub documents the default for omission only ('if omitted, a default message will be used'), and the whole change rests on the difference; it was measured on a real scratch merge before the code was written (merge commit 69dbc1515a554768a00cc4349da0ad3fc4695a21, whose message was its subject line alone) and again at the implementation head.
GitHub appends no second (#n) to a headline it was given: the supplied headline already ended in (#2556) and the merge commit carried exactly one.

enablePullRequestAutoMerge cannot be driven on a scratch base at all. GitHub refuses it on a draft, on an unstable pull request, and on a base with no ruleset ('Protected branch rules not configured for this branch'), and the implement App cannot add a ruleset (403 on POST /rulesets). The arm was therefore proven on this issue's own pull request against main, armed and disarmed in one command with 0 approvals of the 1 main requires.

The package's fake had to record what the mutation's input passes, not what the variables map holds: a variable present in the map but absent from the mutation text is ignored by GraphQL, so a fake keyed on the map alone would stay green while the query sent GitHub nothing.

The pod has no Docker and no PyYAML. internal/daemon's NATS-backed tests cannot run here (LEGION-630), and the repository's yaml-reading check scripts need a python with pyyaml, taken as a uv venv rather than an install into the image.
deviations: The plan's live proof drives the arm on a draft scratch pull request. GitHub refuses that ('Pull request is a draft'), and refuses every other state a scratch base can reach, so the arm was driven on this issue's own pull request against the protected main instead, arming and disarming in one command. The plan foresaw this case and asked that GitHub's answer be recorded either way; the refusals are recorded above and in the pull request body.

The plan's T3 asks for one table covering all three arms plus one case whose fake title differs from the default. The simplify pass found that a separate table restated three rows the existing submission table already asserts once its expectations carry the headline and the body, so the title-varying case is a row of that existing table and the separate test is gone. The coverage is the same; the duplicate execution is not.
openQuestions: O1 (for the architect): this change makes the body key-free; the subject is the pull request's title verbatim, so it is key-free only when the title is. GitHub already writes that title as the subject today (squash_merge_commit_title: COMMIT_OR_PR_TITLE), so this change neither causes nor fixes it. Whether the issue's acceptance should read 'body' where it reads 'message', and where a title check belongs, is the architect's.

O2 (for the architect): the spec cites dispatch://INFRA-472 for 'Stop new leaks only'; that issue is done, closed as dropped at its design gate. The live source of the rule is the controller's relay at dispatch://INFRA-514/comment/fcf8c751.

O3 (for the architect): enablePullRequestAutoMerge stores the headline when it is accepted and GitHub merges later, so a title edited after the arm would merge under the old subject. The daemon disarms on a push but not on a title edit. Recorded, not built.

O4 (for the architect): an empty body drops the Co-authored-by: trailers GitHub writes today. They carry no key, no session id and no skip-checks line, so the spec's rule does not exclude them; the plan follows the spec's 'the body is empty'.

F12 (for the architect): a person's by-hand merge of a MANUAL_MERGE_REQUIRED packet on this repository still takes GitHub's default body. No code of this change reaches that path, and sjawhar/legion#2539 carries the rule into the merger's own command for the paths it owns.
discoveredComplexity: A merge-queue base keeps GitHub's default whatever the daemon sends: EnablePullRequestAutoMergeInput's schema says a commit headline or body input is ignored when merging through a queue, and EnqueuePullRequestInput has no message field at all. main of sjawhar/legion carries no merge-queue rule, so merges here take the arm or the merge; the other repository this project serves does carry one, and it is private.

Driving GitHub's auto-merge arm needs a protected base. That is a property of GitHub's mutation, not of the daemon, and it means no scratch-base harness can ever prove the arm end to end without administration: write.
